stories.summary: IndiGo flight 6E 451 returned to Bengaluru shortly after takeoff on November 7 after a handwritten note threatening a hijack was found in the lavatory. The flight, carrying 178 passengers, was declared a full emergency. Security checks later confirmed the threat was a hoax.

stories.title: British Airways resumes Middle East routes
stories.summary: British Airways is rebuilding its regional network after eight months of disruption to Middle East routes. The airline is resuming flights despite active United States travel advisories. Not every destination is returning at the same pace, and the full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: American Airlines reopens Flagship Dining at LAX
stories.summary: American Airlines has reopened its Flagship Dining facility at Los Angeles International Airport after a six-year hiatus. The service offers table-service, a la carte meals to premium cabin passengers and elite status holders, replacing the previous buffet-style experience. The upgrade is described as a vast improvement.

stories.title: Washington Dulles announces $20 billion expansion
stories.summary: The Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority and United Airlines announced a $20 billion capital investment program for Dulles International Airport. The project covers 5 million square feet of space over the next decade, replacing the existing Concourse C and D. The first piece of the plan arrives within months.

stories.title: Runway construction slows Boston Logan arrivals
stories.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration has restricted incoming traffic at Boston Logan Airport due to ongoing runway and taxiway construction. The ground delay program, which is separate from recent storm-related issues, has resulted in average delays of approximately 70 minutes for affected flights throughout the day.

stories.title: EasyJet flight met by medical services after illness outbreak
stories.summary: An easyJet flight from Hurghada to Edinburgh was met by medical services on November 3 after several passengers developed flu-like symptoms, including vomiting and high temperatures. The crew contacted air traffic control during the journey to report the illness. The airline confirmed the incident upon landing.

stories.title: France investigates potential foreign involvement in airline bomb threats
stories.summary: French authorities are investigating whether a series of recent bomb threats against commercial aircraft are linked to foreign powers. The incidents have forced diversions and security searches across Europe, though no explosive devices have been found. Investigators are currently working to determine if the alerts share a source.

stories.title: Luxury airline cancels November schedule
stories.summary: A luxury airline has cancelled all of its flights scheduled for November and is currently offering refunds to affected passengers. The full details regarding the sudden cessation of operations are available to subscribers.

stories.title: Hoax bomb threats disrupt European flights
stories.summary: A wave of bomb threats has forced diversions, security searches and military escorts for at least 35 aircraft across Europe this week. While no explosive devices have been discovered, the alerts have affected major cities including Milan, Madrid and Vienna. Authorities continue to coordinate a response to the disruptions.

stories.title: Spanish authorities urge calm amid airline bomb threats
stories.summary: Spanish police and air traffic controllers are calling for calm as false bomb threats continue to disrupt aviation. Officials state that the situation is managed through standard procedures and that perpetrators are eventually identified. Airport authority Aena declined to disclose the specific number of threats received for security reasons.

stories.title: Aviation experts label recent bomb threats as exceptional
stories.summary: A series of malicious hoaxes has forced emergency landings and military escorts across European airspace. While no actual attacks have occurred, the incidents have strained the aviation network. Security consultant Wilfried Covent described the scale of the disruption as an exceptional event he has not seen in his career.

stories.title: Airbus and Air France launch component joint venture
stories.summary: Airbus and Air France-KLM have launched Alpha Component Solutions, a joint venture to manage A350 component support. The business begins with contracts covering more than 500 aircraft, providing the planemaker with a guaranteed service base from its first day of operation.

stories.title: Airbus faces year-end delivery challenge
stories.summary: Airbus recorded 202 gross orders in October while delivering 74 jets. To reach its annual target of 870 deliveries, the company must now deliver 249 aircraft over the final two months of the year. Lessors accounted for 185 of the new orders, leaving the production target looking ambitious.

stories.title: AerFin acquires 44 Boeing 737NG aircraft from Qantas
stories.summary: AerFin has purchased 44 Boeing 737NG aircraft and 88 engines from Qantas in the largest transaction in the company history. The aircraft will be transferred over the next seven years to support the aftermarket specialist in providing materials and solutions to global airline and maintenance customers.

stories.title: Boeing forecasts doubling of Chinese commercial fleet
stories.summary: Boeing projects that China's commercial fleet will grow to over 9,800 airplanes within 20 years. The company cites an expanding middle class and increased infrastructure investment as primary drivers for a forecast of 5 percent annual growth in passenger air travel.

stories.title: Boeing reports uneven commercial recovery
stories.summary: Boeing reported third-quarter revenue growth and positive operating cash flow alongside a narrower net loss. The company finalized a large 737-10 order from Avolon while continuing to target stabilized production rates. Performance in defense and services helped offset ongoing pressure within the commercial airplanes division.

stories.title: Airbus secures Spanish C295 order
stories.summary: Spain has ordered 18 C295 aircraft to modernize its air and space forces. The deal adds to the Airbus defense backlog, which has grown steadily throughout the autumn. Separately, the French procurement agency recently qualified the vertical take-off variant of the Aliaca drone for service.

stories.title: Airbus delivery total reaches 621 through October
stories.summary: Airbus delivered 74 aircraft in October, bringing its year-to-date total to 621 jets. The company also reported 202 gross orders for the month, resulting in 1,376 gross orders for the year so far. The manufacturer maintains its annual delivery target despite the remaining volume required.

stories.title: Philippine Airlines expands A350-1000 commitment
stories.summary: Philippine Airlines has finalized an order for nine additional Airbus A350-1000s, bringing its total commitment to 18 aircraft. The contract includes purchase rights for five more jets, with deliveries scheduled between 2034 and 2036 as the airline prepares to renew its long-haul network.

stories.title: IndiGo in talks for large Embraer order
stories.summary: IndiGo is reportedly in early discussions to order as many as 150 regional jets from Embraer. The potential deal includes 100 firm units and 50 options as part of a fleet overhaul. The contract has not been finalized and remains subject to change.

stories.title: Airbus delivery pace trails annual target
stories.summary: Airbus has delivered 621 aircraft through October, a 6.2 percent increase over the same period last year. The company must now deliver 124.5 planes per month in November and December to reach its 870-aircraft target. The manufacturer did not provide comment on the feasibility of the goal.

stories.title: Airbus reports no slowdown in Gulf orders
stories.summary: Airbus states that geopolitical tensions in the Gulf have not impacted airliner orders or deliveries in the region. The company's president for the Middle East and Africa addressed the topic on the sidelines of an industry meeting. Further details on the regional outlook are for subscribers.

stories.title: Airbus October performance leaves year-end target steep
stories.summary: Airbus booked 202 gross orders and delivered 74 jets in October. With 621 deliveries completed year-to-date, the company requires approximately 125 deliveries in each of the final two months to reach its 870-jet target. Leasing companies accounted for the vast majority of the month's new order intake.

stories.title: FAA activates first digital air traffic control towers
stories.summary: The FAA has launched its first digital air traffic control towers in Florida and Alaska. The agency says the camera-based systems provide a continuous 360-degree view of airport operations without replacing human controllers. Five additional airports are slated to receive the technology as part of a wider modernization effort.

stories.title: FAA announces first US digital air traffic control towers in Florida and Alaska
stories.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced that the first digital air traffic control towers in the US are officially operational, bringing new technology first to smaller airports in Florida and Alaska as the Trump administration presses ahead with updating the country’s ageing aviation infrastructure.

stories.summary: WASHINGTON , The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said November 6 that digital air traffic control towers are operational at Bartow Executive Airport (BOW) in Florida and Kenai Municipal Airport (ENA) in Alaska, expanding its deployment of camera-based systems for controllers. stories.title: FAA to replace floppy disks in air traffic control by 2028
stories.summary: The FAA plans to retire 1980s-era information systems across 435 facilities by 2028. The agency is replacing floppy disks with the Enterprise Information Display System to centralize flight alerts and weather data. The FAA describes the transition as a historic modernization of the country’s air traffic control infrastructure.

stories.title: Uttarakhand helicopter operators suspend charter services
stories.summary: Helicopter operators in Uttarakhand have grounded all Char Dham charter services following a regulatory mandate for twin-pilot operations. The directive was issued after an October 30 crash killed six people. Operators have filed a joint representation to the DGCA to object to the new safety requirement.

stories.summary: Airbus has launched new digital courseware through its Skywise platform and signed a pilot training agreement with Blue Angels Air in India. While the company expands its aviation training footprint, analysts at UBS have cut their price target for the stock.

stories.title: TUI offers conditional jobs to new pilot recruits
stories.summary: TUI Airways has partnered with Leading Edge Aviation to offer conditional employment to students before they begin flight training. The integrated program starts in February 2027, with type rating courses scheduled for December 2028. Applicants can apply for the pathway starting this month.

stories.summary: US private equity group Excolere Equity Partners has acquired flight training company Skyborne Airline Academy. While the company initially described the deal as a significant investment, an email to suppliers confirmed the transaction was a full purchase. The acquisition closed on October 29.

stories.title: Defence ministry clears pilot training institute at Darbhanga airport
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Defence has issued a no objection certificate for a flying training organisation at Darbhanga Airport. Bihar officials say the move will boost local aviation careers and reduce dependence on metro-based facilities. The project now awaits further operational approvals to begin training local pilots.

stories.title: Kuwaiti cadets begin pilot training in Spain
stories.summary: BAA Training has partnered with Jazeera Airways to provide an 18-month integrated pilot license course for Kuwaiti cadets. The first group began training in August 2026 at the company's facilities in Lleida-Alguaire, Spain. The program includes multi-crew cooperation training as the airline expands its fleet.

stories.title: High operations tempo impacts U.S. Air Force mobility fleet
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force has adjusted its maintenance posture to sustain a high operations tempo for its mobility aircraft during ongoing missions in Iran and elsewhere. The full report on how these flight demands are impacting the service is available to subscribers of Aviation Week.

stories.title: Air Force launches B-1B pilot training program
stories.summary: The Air Force has introduced a new training program for B-1B pilots intended to increase total flight hours. The initiative aims to address pilot readiness through an updated curriculum. The full details of the program are available to subscribers of Aviation News.eu.
